title.narrative: Strengthening the quality and scale of preventative nutrition services for most vulnerable groups through community management of acute malnutrition in Borno State

description.narrative: ltpgtltbrgtThis project targets vulnerable communities in Maiduguri Metropolitan Council (MMC) and Jere Local Government Areas of Borno state, which are severely affected by acute malnutrition. The primary objective is to prevent and manage Severe Acute Malnutrition (SAM) by enhancing community-based interventions aimed at improving the health and well-being of children under five, pregnant and breastfeeding women and girls, thereby reducing the morbidity and mortality associated with Global Acute Malnutrition (GAM).ltbrgtThe intervention will be driven by Community Nutrition Mobilizers, who will lead extensive community sensitization and active case finding to identify and refer SAM cases to UNICEF supported Government Outpatient Therapeutic Programmes (OTPs) and stabilization centers for appropriate care. The project will also support the treatment of Moderate Acute Malnutrition (MAM) in children aged 6–59 months through the distribution of Tom Brown and/or Ready to Use Supplementary Food (RUSF)ltbrgtMaternal, Infant, and Young Child Nutrition (MIYCN) counseling services will be provided, alongside supplementary nutrition assistance for children under five, as well as pregnant and breastfeeding women and girls. Community members will be trained on Infant and Young Child Feeding (IYCF) practices and the use of Mid-Upper Arm Circumference (MUAC) tapes to strengthen local capacity for accurate screening, timely detection, and appropriate referral of SAM cases.ltbrgtTo enhance access to treatment and promote adherence, the project will incorporate Cash and Voucher Assistance (CVA). Gender-Based Violence (GBV) and Protection from Sexual Exploitation and Abuse (PSEA) awareness sessions will also be conducted to ensure the safe and timely referral of women and girls to specialized support services.ltbrgtThe project will further strengthen community ownership through the establishment and support of local nutrition groups, empowering them to continuously monitor, identify, and refer new malnutrition cases. Additionally, capacity-building initiatives will be implemented for government healthcare providers to ensure sustainability and improved service delivery. ltbrgtlt/pgt
